question: A raised wheal appearing along a firm stroke line on the forearm confirms that the patient has symptomatic dermographism requiring treatment with an antihistamine.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: A wheal without itch is simple (asymptomatic) dermographism, found in approximately one in twenty healthy people, and requires only reassurance — not medication. It is the presence of pruritus accompanying the wheal that defines symptomatic dermographism and warrants treatment. Always ask the patient 'Does this itch?' while the wheal is rising before deciding whether treatment is needed.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — a wheal alone does not confirm symptomatic dermographism. Simple (asymptomatic) dermographism — a wheal without itch — occurs in about 5% of healthy people and needs only reassurance, not medication. The crucial question is whether the wheal itches: only a wheal accompanied by pruritus constitutes symptomatic dermographism warranting treatment with a second-generation antihistamine.
